chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Miskan, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him).

Regarding the Words of Allah the Exalted: 'It is made lawful to you to go to your wives on the night of the Fast' — the Verse. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It was revealed regarding Khawwat ibn Jubayr al-Ansari, and he was with the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) during the Khandaq (Battle of the Ditch), and he was fasting. So evening came and he was upon that state, and it was such that before the revelation of this Verse, whenever one of them fell asleep, the food and drink was prohibited upon him. So Khawwat went to his family when it was evening, so he said, 'Is there any food with you?' So they said, 'No, do not sleep until we prepare food for you.' So he reclined and fell asleep. So they said to him, 'You have done it (fallen asleep)?' He said, 'Yes.' So he spent the night upon that state. So in the morning, he went to the ditch, and fainting overcame him. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by him. So when he saw that which was with him, he informed him of how his matter was. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Verse regarding him: 'And eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread at Dawn'.

key_terms.خَوَّاتُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ: Khawwat ibn Jubayr (the companion mentioned in the narrative)
key_terms.يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ: Until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread (metaphor for dawn)

ai.seo_question: What is the historical context behind the verse 'Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread'?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the historical context of the revelation of Surah Al-Baqarah 2:187, specifically addressing the case of Khawwat ibn Jubayr during the Battle of the Ditch. It highlights the transition from a strict pre-revelation ruling, where sleep prohibited eating, to the clarified permission to consume food and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black, demonstrating the divine easing of hardship for the believers.
